extracted.intended_audience: Applicants, licensees, and counsel participating in FCC spectrum auctions or seeking designated-entity/small-business benefits (including consortium members, rural service providers, and tribal land bidders).
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and procedures for determining designated-entity (small business, rural service provider, tribal/other) eligibility, attribution/affiliation rules, and bidding-credit provisions in FCC spectrum auctions. Covers definitions, aggregation/attribution rules, exceptions, bidding-credit formulas, certifications, and penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for evaluating eligibility for small business benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for small business benefits: (i) an applicant must meet the applicable small business size standard in paragraphs (b)(1) and (2) of this section; and (ii) must retain de jure and de facto control over the spectrum associated with the license(s) for which it seeks small business benefits. An applicant or licensee may lose eligibility for size-based benefits for one or more licenses without losing general eligibility for size-based benefits so long as it retains de jure and de facto control of its overall business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retaining both legal (de jure) and actual (de facto) control is required. Eligibility can be lost for particular licenses but maintained generally if overall control is preserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation/attribution where persons treated as one entity (identity of interest/affiliate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where individuals/entities have an identity of interest or are affiliates, their separate interests in an applicant must be aggregated. (Example: A & B who together control ABC Corp. and have an identity of interest — A & B's separate interests in DE Corp. must be aggregated.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes parent-subsidiary situations (ABC Corp. and BC Corp. investing separately in DE Corp. are aggregated as affiliates). Use these rules to determine whether multiple related parties are treated as one person for eligibility/attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consortium exception to aggregation
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an applicant is a consortium of entities eligible for size-based bidding credits and/or closed bidding based on gross revenues and/or total assets, the gross revenues and/or total assets of each consortium member shall not be aggregated. For rural service provider bidding credits, the subscribers of each consortium member shall not be aggregated. Each consortium member must constitute a separate and distinct legal entity to qualify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consortia that are winning bidders using this exception must comply with § 1.2107(g) as a condition of license grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicants without identifiable controlling interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an applicant (or licensee) cannot identify controlling interests under the standards set forth in this section, the gross revenues of all interest holders in the applicant, and their affiliates, will be attributable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If control cannot be determined under the rules, conservative attribution of all interest-holders' gross revenues applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rural telephone cooperative exception criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant (or controlling interest) will be exempt from § 1.2110(c)(2)(ii)(F) for attribution if it: (i) is organized as a cooperative pursuant to state law; (ii) is a 'rural telephone company' as defined by the Communications Act; and (iii) demonstrates either eligibility for tax-exempt status under the Internal Revenue Code or adherence to cooperative principles articulated in Puget Sound Plywood, Inc. v. Commissioner of Internal Revenue, 44 T.C. 305 (1965).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no state organic statute exists, applicant must show valid organization and organic documents indicating cooperative operation. If controlling interest is not an eligible rural telephone cooperative, § (a) applies with respect to relevant officers/directors unless controlled by or an eligible cooperative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of small businesses (service-specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will establish the definition of a small business on a service-specific basis, taking into consideration the characteristics and capital requirements of the particular service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Size standards vary by service; consult service-specific rules for exact thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controlling interests — de jure and de facto control
rubrics_metrics.description: Controlling interest includes individuals or entities with either de jure or de facto control. De jure control is evidenced by holdings of greater than 50 percent of the voting stock of a corporation or, in a partnership, general partnership interests. De facto control is determined case-by-case; an entity must disclose its equity interest and demonstrate indicia of control including: (A) constituting or appointing more than 50 percent of the board of directors/management committee; (B) authority to appoint, promote, demote, and fire senior executives controlling day-to-day activities; and (C) playing an integral role in management decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishing de facto control requires demonstrating one or more indicia. Disclosure of equity interest is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fully diluted calculation of ownership interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Ownership interests shall be calculated on a fully diluted basis; all agreements such as warrants, stock options and convertible debentures will generally be treated as if the rights thereunder already have been fully exercised, except as set forth in paragraph (c)(2)(ii)(A)(2). Rights of first refusal and put options shall not be calculated on a fully diluted basis for determining de jure control but shall be calculated on a fully diluted basis if such interests, in combination with other terms, deprive an otherwise qualified applicant or licensee of de facto control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mutually exclusive contingent ownership interests are calculated only in possible combinations in which they can be exercised. Look for contractual language specifying exclusivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation and attribution of partnership and other ownership interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Partnership and other ownership interests and any stock interest (equity, outstanding stock, or outstanding voting stock) shall be attributed as specified in the attribution rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the detailed attribution provisions in (c)(2)(ii)(B)-(J) for different ownership types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution of stock interests held in trust
rubrics_metrics.description: Stock interests held in trust shall be attributed to any person who holds or shares the power to vote such stock, to any person who has the sole power to sell such stock, and to any person who has the right to revoke the trust at will or to replace the trustee at will.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the trustee has familial, personal, or extra-trust business relationship to grantor or beneficiary, the grantor or beneficiary will be attributed with the stock interests held in trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-voting stock attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-voting stock shall be attributed as an interest in the issuing entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-voting shares count for attribution purposes even if they lack voting rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited partnership interests attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Limited partnership interests shall be attributed to limited partners and shall be calculated according to both the percentage of equity paid in and the percentage of distribution of profits and losses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both capital contribution percentages and profit/loss distribution are used in attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Officers and directors considered controlling interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Officers and directors of the applicant shall be considered to have a controlling interest in the applicant. Officers/directors of an entity that controls a licensee or applicant shall be considered to have a controlling interest in the licensee or applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal net worth/income of officers/directors is not attributed; however, gross revenues of affiliates of officers/directors are attributable to the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect ownership through intervening corporations
rubrics_metrics.description: Ownership interests held indirectly through one or more intervening corporations will be determined by successive multiplication of ownership percentages for each link in the vertical ownership chain and application of the relevant attribution benchmark to the resulting product; if any link exceeds 50 percent or represents actual control, it shall be treated as if it were a 100 percent interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiply percentages along chain; treat >50% at any link as full ownership for attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management agreements creating controlling interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who manages the operations of an applicant or licensee pursuant to a management agreement shall be considered to have a controlling interest if such person, or its affiliate, has authority to make decisions or otherwise engage in practices or activities that determine, or significantly influence: (1) the nature or types of services offered; (2) the terms upon which such services are offered; or (3) the prices charged for such services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantial operational decision authority under a management agreement can create attribution even without equity ownership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint marketing arrangements attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Any licensee or its affiliate who enters into a joint marketing arrangement with an applicant or licensee, or its affiliate, shall be considered to have a controlling interest if such applicant or licensee, or its affiliate, has authority to make decisions or otherwise engage in practices or activities that determine or significantly influence the nature/types of services, terms, or prices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look to authority to determine service nature, terms, or prices when assessing attribution from marketing arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosable interest holder spectrum-use attribution (25% rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: For bidding-credit purposes, the gross revenues (or, for rural service providers, the subscribers) of any disclosable interest holder are attributable to the applicant/licensee on a license-by-license basis if the disclosable interest holder uses, or has an agreement to use, more than 25 percent of the spectrum capacity of a license awarded with bidding credits. A disclosable interest holder is any individual or entity holding a ten percent or greater interest of any kind in the designated entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule does not cause a disclosable interest holder not otherwise controlling/affiliate to make its subscribers attributable to a rural service provider if: (1) the disclosable holder is independently eligible for a rural service provider bidding credit; and (2) the spectrum use and agreements are otherwise permissible under Commission rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of businesses owned by minorities and/or women
rubrics_metrics.description: A business owned by members of minority groups and/or women is one in which minorities and/or women who are U.S. citizens control the applicant, have at least greater than 50 percent equity ownership and, for corporate applicants, have a greater than 50 percent voting interest. For partnerships, every general partner must be a minority and/or woman U.S. citizen who individually or together own at least 50 percent of partnership equity, or an entity 100 percent owned and controlled by minorities and/or women who are U.S. citizens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interests are calculated on a fully diluted basis (options, convertible debentures treated as exercised), though a waiver of fully-diluted calculation may be sought upon demonstration that options/conversion rights held by non-controlling principals will not deprive minority/female principals of substantial financial stake or control. 'Minority' includes specified racial/ethnic groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of rural telephone company
rubrics_metrics.description: A rural telephone company is any local exchange carrier operating entity to the extent that such entity: (i) provides common carrier service to any local exchange carrier study area that does not include any incorporated place of 10,000 inhabitants or more (or part thereof) or any territory included in an urbanized area as of Aug 10, 1993; (ii) provides telephone exchange service to fewer than 50,000 access lines; (iii) provides telephone exchange service to any LEC study area with fewer than 100,000 access lines; or (iv) has less than 15 percent of its access lines in communities of more than 50,000 on the date of enactment of the Telecommunications Act of 1996.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple alternative metrics can qualify an entity as a rural telephone company; check applicable service/date references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliate definition
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual or entity is an affiliate of an applicant or of a person holding an attributable interest in an applicant if such individual or entity: (A) directly or indirectly controls or has the power to control the applicant; (B) is directly or indirectly controlled by the applicant; (C) is directly or indirectly controlled by a third party or parties that also controls or has the power to control the applicant; or (D) has an 'identity of interest' with the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affiliation is broad and includes direct, indirect, and identity-of-interest relationships; apply the 'nature of control' rules to determine affiliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature of control — affirmative/negative and existence of power to control
rubrics_metrics.description: Every business concern is considered to have one or more parties who directly or indirectly control or have the power to control it. Control may be affirmative or negative and it is immaterial whether it is exercised so long as the power to control exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: owning 50% voting stock gives negative power to control; bylaws may give a minority stockholder blocking power. Presence of power (not exercise) is dispositive for affiliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control via stock ownership, positions, contractual relations, or combination
rubrics_metrics.description: Control can arise through stock ownership; occupancy of director, officer or key employee positions; contractual or other business relations; or combinations of these and other factors. A key employee is one who, because of position, has critical influence or substantive control over operations/management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess multiple factors — not merely equity percentages — to determine control. Management positions can create affiliation even with dispersed stock.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity of interest between/among persons (family/common investments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Affiliation can arise between or among two or more persons with an identity of interest, such as members of the same family or persons with common investments; persons with an identity of interest will be treated as though they were one person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joint investments or family ties creating common economic interests lead to aggregation/attribution; examples show two shareholders treated as one person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spousal and kinship affiliation presumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Spouses are deemed to own or control interests owned/controlled by either of them unless legally separated in a U.S. recognized court. Immediate family members are presumed to own/control interests of other immediate family members; 'immediate family' is defined (father, mother, husband, wife, son, daughter, brother, sister, parents-/in-laws, step- relatives, half-siblings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presumptions may be rebutted by showing estrangement, remote family ties, or lack of business involvement. Example: an attributable interest may be attributed through kinship unless rebutted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliation presumptions from stock ownership sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant is presumed to control a concern if he/she owns or controls 50 percent or more of its voting stock. An applicant is presumed to control even with less than 50 percent if the block is large compared to any other outstanding block. If two or more persons each own less than 50 percent but minority holdings are equal/approximately equal and together form a large aggregate, presumption arises that each individually controls unless rebutted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are rebuttable presumptions; evidence can be presented to show lack of actual control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliation arising under stock options, convertible debentures, and agreements to merge
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as set forth for certain exceptions, stock options, convertible debentures, and agreements to merge are generally considered to have a present effect on the power to control and are treated as though rights had been exercised. Example: option to purchase a controlling interest is treated as though exercised; an agreement to merge is treated as though merger has taken place. However, some examples show when options are not considered to have present effect to prevent circumvention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat contingent instruments as exercised for size determination unless specific exception applies; review examples showing when an option is/ isn't given present effect. Note the mutually exclusive contingent ownership interests rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliation under voting trusts
rubrics_metrics.description: Stock interests held in trust are deemed controlled by any person who holds or shares the power to vote such stock, has sole power to sell such stock, or has the right to revoke the trust at will or replace the trustee at will. If the trustee has familial/personal/extra-trust business relationship to grantor or beneficiary, stock interests are deemed controlled by grantor/beneficiary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voting trusts intended primarily to shift control to meet size standards are invalid for this purpose regardless of jurisdictional recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliation through common management
rubrics_metrics.description: Affiliation generally arises where officers, directors, or key employees serve as the majority or otherwise as the controlling element of the board of directors and/or management of another entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overlap in management personnel that yields control can create affiliation even without ownership ties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliation through common facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Affiliation generally arises where one concern shares office space and/or employees and/or other facilities with another concern, particularly where such concerns are in the same or related industry or field of operations, or were formerly affiliated, and through these sharing arrangements one concern has control, or potential control, of the other concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shared facilities that create operational dependence or control factor into affiliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliation through contractual relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Affiliation generally arises where one concern is dependent upon another concern for contracts and business to such a degree that one concern has control, or potential control, of the other concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine contractual dependence and its practical effect on control when assessing affiliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliation under joint venture arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: A joint venture for size determination purposes is an association of concerns and/or individuals formed by contract to engage in a single, specific business venture for joint profit where they combine efforts/property/money/skill and knowledge, not on a continuing or permanent basis. Parties to a joint venture are considered to be affiliated with each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joint venture parties are affiliated for attribution purposes. This subsection does not define small business consortium for designated-entity status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion from affiliation coverage — Indian tribes and ANCSA entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Indian tribes or Alaska Regional or Village Corporations organized pursuant to the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act, or entities owned and controlled by such tribes/corporations, are not considered affiliates of an applicant (or licensee) that is owned and controlled by such tribes/corporations and otherwise complies, except that gross revenues derived from gaming activities conducted by affiliate entities pursuant to the Indian Gaming Regulatory Act will be counted in determining compliance unless applicant establishes it will not receive substantial unfair competitive advantage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tribal/ANCSA ownership generally avoids affiliation attribution except for gaming revenues unless mitigated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consortium definition (small business/very small/entrepreneur/rural)
rubrics_metrics.description: A consortium of small businesses, very small businesses, entrepreneurs, or rural service providers is a conglomerate organization composed of two or more entities, each of which individually satisfies the definition of a small business, very small business, entrepreneur, or rural service provider as defined in this section and in applicable service-specific rules. Each individual member must constitute a separate and distinct legal entity to qualify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consortium members must individually qualify and be distinct legal entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission may set aside licenses for designated entities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may set aside specific licenses for which only eligible designated entities, as specified by the Commission, may bid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set-asides are a discretionary tool; check service-specific competitive bidding rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission may permit partitioning of service areas for eligible designated entities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may permit partitioning of service areas in particular services for eligible designated entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partitioning can be used to facilitate designated-entity participation; see service-specific rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bidding credits — general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may award bidding credits (i.e., payment discounts) to eligible designated entities. Competitive bidding rules applicable to individual services will specify the designated entities eligible for bidding credits, the licenses for which bidding credits are available, the amounts of bidding credits and other procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult competitive bidding rules for service-specific eligibility and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small business bidding credits — size tiers and percentages
rubrics_metrics.description: A winning bidder that qualifies as a small business (and has not claimed a rural service provider bidding credit) may use bidding credits corresponding to its respective average gross revenues for the preceding 5 years: (A) average gross revenues ≤ $4 million → 35%; (B) ≤ $20 million → 25%; (C) ≤ $55 million → 15%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Average gross revenues are taken over the preceding 5 years; these tiers determine percentage discounts on payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cap on winning bid discount (auction-by-auction)
rubrics_metrics.description: A maximum total discount that a winning bidder eligible for a small business bidding credit may receive will be established on an auction-by-auction basis. The limit on the discount will be no less than $25 million. The Commission may adopt a market-based cap on an auction-by-auction basis establishing an overall limit on the discount for certain license areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if percentage credits suggest larger discounts, the auction-specific cap applies; minimum cap is $25M.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of qualifying tribal land for bidding credit
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualifying tribal land means any federally recognized Indian tribe's reservation, Pueblo, or Colony, including former reservations in Oklahoma, Alaska Native regions established pursuant to the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act, and Indian allotments, that has a wireline telephone subscription rate equal to or less than eighty-five (85) percent based on the most recently available U.S. Census Data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualification depends on current census-based subscription rates and formal tribal/geographic definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tribal land certification requirements (within 180 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 180 days after the filing deadline for long-form applications, the winning bidder must amend its long-form application and attach a certification from the tribal government that: (1) the tribal government authorizes siting and service; (2) the tribal area constitutes qualifying tribal land; and (3) the tribal government has not and will not enter an exclusive contract precluding entry or unreasonably discriminate among carriers. Additionally, the winning bidder must file a certification that it will comply with construction requirements and consult with the tribal government regarding siting and deployment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to submit required certifications within 180 days results in loss of the tribal bidding credit and obligation to pay outstanding bid balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tribal land bidding credit formula
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to applicable bidding credit limits, the bidding credit equals $500,000 for the first 200 square miles (518 sq km) of qualifying tribal land, and $2,500 for each additional square mile (2.590 sq km) of qualifying tribal land above 200 square miles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute total tribal land area served under the license to apply the formula; be mindful of caps that may reduce actual credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tribal land bidding credit limit (caps by high bid amount)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the high bid is ≤ $1,000,000, the maximum tribal credit shall not exceed 50% of the high bid. If the high bid is > $1,000,000 and ≤ $2,000,000, the maximum tribal credit shall not exceed $500,000. If the high bid is > $2,000,000, the maximum tribal credit shall not exceed 35% of the high bid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These caps may reduce the tribal land credit calculated by the formula; check the high bid to determine applicable cap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bidding credit limit in auctions subject to reserve prices — pro rata allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: In auctions with reserve prices where this provision applies, the aggregate amount available as tribal land bidding credits for licenses subject to a reserve price shall not exceed the amount by which winning bids (net of discounts the Commission counts when reporting net bids) exceed the applicable reserve price. If requested credits exceed available aggregate amount, the Commission will award eligible applicants a pro rata tribal land bidding credit, calculated by multiplying the full credit by a fraction (numerator: amount by which winning bids net of discounts exceed reserve price; denominator: aggregate maximum tribal credits applicants might have qualified for).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission will recalculate pro rata credits after final resolution of all applications seeking tribal credits for such licenses; final determinations occur after review/reconsideration processes conclude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application and timing of tribal land bidding credit
rubrics_metrics.description: A pending request for a tribal bidding credit has no effect on a bidder's obligations to make auction payments prior to award of the credit. Tribal land bidding credits will be calculated and awarded prior to license grant. If a pro rata credit is granted prior to license grant, the Commission shall recalculate after all applications are finally resolved; if recalculated credit is larger, the Commission will award the difference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on prospective credits to reduce required payments until the Commission awards them; credits are reconciled prior to grant and may be increased after final resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-construction certification for tribal land bidding credit
rubrics_metrics.description: Within fifteen (15) days of the third anniversary of the initial grant of its license, a recipient of a tribal bidding credit must file a certification that it has constructed and is operating a system capable of serving 75% of the population of the qualifying tribal land for which the credit was awarded, and provide total population and number of persons served.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification must be timely and include population metrics; failure triggers penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance penalties for failure to meet tribal construction/certification
rubrics_metrics.description: If a recipient fails to provide the required post-construction certification, it shall repay the bidding credit amount in its entirety, plus interest (based on the rate for ten-year U.S. Treasury obligations applicable on the date the license is granted). Payment must be made within 30 days of the third anniversary of the initial grant; failure to repay results in automatic termination of the license. Repayment does not affect calculation of amounts available to be awarded as tribal land bidding credits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalties are strict: repayment plus interest and possible automatic license termination for nonpayment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rural service provider bidding credit — eligibility and definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A winning bidder that qualifies as a rural service provider and has not claimed a small business bidding credit will be eligible for a 15% bidding credit. A rural service provider means a service provider that: (A) is in the business of providing commercial communications services and together with its controlling interests, affiliates, and affiliates of its controlling interests has fewer than 250,000 combined wireless, wireline, broadband, and cable subscribers as of the short-form filing deadline; and (B) serves predominantly rural areas, defined as counties with a population density of 100 or fewer persons per square mile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subscriber counts are aggregated with controlling interests and affiliates as defined elsewhere; the short-form filing deadline is the relevant date for subscriber totals.
